rationale: Budgets are gates, not estimates. They are enforced by harness doctor and harness budget so that a limit which is only documented cannot quietly decay.

hot.note: Single-file manifests stop being read reliably past roughly 3000 tokens. Keep this one small enough that it is always fully honoured.

warm.note: A skill over budget is a signal to split it, not to raise the number. Payload reduction of about a third is typically available with no measurable quality loss.

cold.note: MCP tool catalogues are paid for on connection. Enable only the servers a workflow actually uses.

targets.note: The gap between these two numbers is context engineering, not model choice.

rules: alwaysApply true requires a written justification in the skill frontmatter
no timestamp, request id or generated header in the cached prefix
prefer one focused skill over a large one that activates on a broad glob
load the large reference on demand rather than inlining it in every turn
a verification result holds until the tree changes: record what ran and the tree state, and do not re-run it for the same state
a problem that predates the change is a warn, never an extra round
prefer a connected token-saving MCP server such as cross-tk for reads, searches and summaries; never probe for one that is absent
